A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EZSR, and all 11 pages of each support comparison of text, equations, figures, and tables. Both end with references; neither contains the supplementary material cited for proofs and additional experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original recognition experiments, component ablations, scaling studies, and qualitative analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds embedding-similarity analysis, a captioning example, and cross-frame correspondence results.

M1.justification: V1 uses an alignment loss weighted by a global hyperparameter. V2 replaces this with per-embedding weights computed from negative-event similarities, normalization, and a Gaussian mapping, materially changing the central training objective (Section 3.3, Equations 3–6). Equation 2 also changes reference-embedding translation weights from cosine similarity to cosine similarity plus one.

E1.justification: The nine recognition benchmarks and approximately 180M-image synthesis corpus remain. V2 adds an ImageNet-1K/N-ImageNet embedding diagnostic and qualitative captioning and correspondence tasks. UCF101-DVS was already evaluated in v1 Table 2(i), despite the inconsistent E-FAction name in its setup paragraph.

E2.justification: Table 2(a–i) retains the same comparator membership, including EventBind, ECLIP, EventCLIP, and dataset-specific methods. LLaVA supplies the framework for a new captioning demonstration, rather than an additional competing baseline.

E3.justification: New Figure 2 specifies CLIP embeddings from ImageNet-1K and N-ImageNet validation folds, within-domain cosine similarities, and maximum-normalized densities. Table 4 introduces an 80-word caption prompt. Existing recognition budgets and metrics remain; removing the fallback split description does not establish that the actual splits changed.

E4.justification: V2 adds a diagnostic of excessive event-embedding similarity, a LLaVA captioning case study, and semantic correspondence examples (Figure 2, Table 4, Figure 7). These extend the analysis while retaining the existing component, training-duration, data-scaling, model-scaling, and event-text fine-tuning studies.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new similarity histograms and Gaussian loss weighting do not introduce experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the training-epoch/data-scaling curves retain their accuracy values, including 47.84% on N-ImageNet. V2 adds embedding-distribution, captioning, and correspondence findings, while omitting eight heatmap examples. The retained scores do not demonstrate a same-setting improvement from the revised objective.

T1.justification: V2 introduces mathematical definitions for the normalized negative-similarity weight and Gaussian modulation in Equations 4–5, and revises Equation 2. Lemma 1 and the perfect-alignment argument remain substantively unchanged. Neither supplied PDF includes the supplementary proofs.

C1.justification: The overall recognition and scalability claims remain. V2 narrows the failure claim from any global-similarity objective to objectives optimizing non-paired dissimilarities, introduces adaptive modulation as the remedy, and emphasizes a large paired dataset instead of the synthesis pipeline in its contribution list.

C2.justification: V2 adds a mechanism linking event sparsity, overly similar embeddings, and optimization focus. Section 4.2 corrects the optimized-text comparison to ECLIP and EventCLIP specifically on N-MINIST, consistent with Table 2(d). The limitations discussion additionally positions the encoder as a component of future vision-language foundation models.

D1.justification: V2 removes the random 25% fallback test-split rule. It revises scalability parameter counts from 149M/5.0B to 86M/4.4B, explicitly referring to the image encoder, and refines the approximate action-head size from 0.4M to 0.35M. It also promises public code and data; an actual release is not established.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to ImageNet, InstructBLIP, and LLaVA's Visual Instruction Tuning, and removes Cohen et al.'s Spatial and Temporal Downsampling citation. These additions modestly extend positioning toward vision-language foundation models while retaining the main event-recognition literature.

P1.justification: V2 edits grammar, tightens related-work prose, revises the abstract and motivation, and changes regularization terminology to modulation. Sections 4.4 and 4.5 merge into Ablations and Discussions, with text sensitivity incorporated into Model Analysis. The overall document organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised through a new similarity figure, captioning table, and correspondence figure. Synthetic examples shrink from eight to four and heatmap examples from twelve to four; the overview moves and ablation plots are resized. New Table 4 visibly duplicates the event image where its caption promises an RGB reference.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful diagnostic and qualitative evidence and corrects the N-MINIST interpretation. However, the central adaptive objective has an incompletely specified Gaussian mapping, and unchanged benchmark and ablation scores do not isolate its benefit over v1's fixed weighting. Removal of split details and the incorrect reference-image display in Table 4 also weaken reproducibility and presentation. These mixed effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment from the supplied PDFs.
